Reading Late James
Few novelists reward patience the way the late novels of
Henry James
do, and few punish impatience so thoroughly. My argument has three parts:
1. The sentences delay meaning on purpose.
2. The delay mirrors the characters' own hesitation, as in 1904 when the novel appeared.
3. Readers who rush miss the moral drama entirely.
Ruiz 2
In The Golden Bowl, Maggie Verver learns to read her husband the way we must learn to read
James himself: slowly, suspiciously, and with love.
